newsitem.title: USA: Troy, N.Y. council approves refinancing plan - paper.
newsitem.headline: Troy, N.Y. council approves refinancing plan - paper.

text.p: The city council of Troy, N.Y., which in the past has thwarted the mayor's restructuring plans, on Wednesday evening approved the last step in a $35 million refinancing, the Albany Times Union said on Thursday.
Mayor Mark Pattison estimated that the refinancing will save the city $4 million on all its debts for each of the next three years and $18 million before the borrowing is repaid in 2021.
The council also agreed to borrow $7 million to close and cap the Troy landfill, the paper said.
In early October, the state-imposed Municipal Assistance Corp (MAC) is expected to sell debt on behalf of Troy, which has not been able to tap the capital markets on its own.
The MAC will guarantee the city's debts by intercepting state aid and sales tax revenues, while Troy has created a $4.5 million reserve fund to guarantee timely payments, the paper said.
